material_units.source_text: (a) $\cos$ decreases on $[0,\pi/2]\supseteq J$, so $\cos(J)=[\cos1,\cos(\cos1)]=[0.5403,0.8576]\subseteq J$. By the mean value theorem $|\cos x-\cos y|=|\sin\xi|\,|x-y|\le\sin1\,|x-y|$ on $J$, so $L=0.8415$; $J$ is closed, and Banach gives the unique fixed point $x^\ast=0.739085$. (b) $|x_1-x_0|=|0.5403-1|=0.4597$ and $1-L=0.1585$: $k\ge\ln\big(0.4597/(0.1585\cdot10^{-6})\big)/\ln(1/0.8415)=14.88/0.1726=86.2$, so $87$. (c) $L$ is the worst slope on $J$, but near $x^\ast$ the slope is $\sin x^\ast=0.674$; with $|x_0-x^\ast|=0.261$ this predicts $\ln(0.261\cdot10^6)/\ln(1/0.674)=31.6$, i.e. $32$. The bound must hold for every start in $J$. (d) $\frac{L}{1-L}|x_{10}-x_9|=5.31\cdot0.012833=0.068$, against the true error $0.0052$ and the a priori bound $0.52$ at $k=10$.
